challenges.name: thin-controllers-quiz
challenges.title: Read the controllers: a deny-list response and a rule that lives in two places
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the CodeDev API: a profile handler that deletes one field before returning a database row, and an enrollment rule copied into two controllers that drifted apart.

questions.explanation: False. The handler returns the whole row minus one named field, so every column added later is published by default: after the migration the response contains mfaSecret, and the test still passes because it only checks the one field somebody remembered. That is a deny-list. The safe shape is an allow-list: map the entity to a response DTO that names exactly the public fields (id, displayName, avatarUrl, joinedAt), and test the exact set of keys (`expect(Object.keys(res).sort()).toEqual([...])`), which fails as soon as anything new appears. The misconception is that a test for the known leak protects against the next one.

True. The two endpoints disagree because each controller holds its own copy of the rule, and only one copy was updated when beta courses were added. Once the rule lives in the service and both controllers only map their input (the session user, or a CSV row) to the same enroll() call, there is one implementation, so one unit test of the service with a fake repository checks what both endpoints do, and a future change to the rule cannot reach only one of them. The controllers still need a small test each for their own mapping, such as where the user id comes from. The misconception is that copying a small if-statement is harmless; copies of business rules drift.

challenges.name: thin-controller-handlers
challenges.title: Write thin controller handlers
challenges.description: Two CodeDev controllers had drifted (each held its own copy of an enrollment rule) and GET /users/:id/profile returned a whole user row, passwordHash included. The service is now the only place for rules; your job is the controller around it. The starter contains CatalogService (already written, do not change) and an empty CodeDevController with three handlers. A request is { params, query, body, user } with string query and params values; a response is { status, headers, body }. Each handler maps the request, calls the service once, and maps the result; a 400 never calls the service. listCourses (GET /courses): query page (default 1) and limit (default 20) must be digits only and at least 1, otherwise 400 "page must be a positive integer" / "limit must be a positive integer"; a limit above 50 becomes 50; level is optional and must be exactly "beginner", "intermediate" or "advanced", otherwise 400 "level must be one of: beginner, intermediate, advanced"; check page, limit, level in that order. Call service.listCourses({ page, limit, level }) and answer 200 with headers { "X-Total-Count": String(total) } and body { items: [{ id, title, level, priceVnd }], page, limit, total }. enroll (POST /enrollments): the body must be an object (not null, not an array) whose courseId is a string, otherwise 400 "courseId is required"; the learner is req.user.id, never a userId sent in the body; call service.enroll({ userId, courseId }) and answer 201 with headers { Location: "/enrollments/<id>" } and body { id, courseId, status, createdAt }. getProfile (GET /users/:id/profile): call service.getProfile(req.params.id); null is 404 with body { error: "user not found" }; otherwise 200 with body { id, displayName, avatarUrl, joinedAt } where joinedAt is the user's createdAt. Every 400 has headers {} and body { error: "<message>" }; 200 and 404 from getProfile have headers {}. Bodies contain exactly the listed fields: never passwordHash, email, role, internalNotes, paymentRef, published or authorPayoutPercent. Input (stdin): { courses? | generateCourses?, users?, requests: [{ route, query?, params?, body?, user? }] }. For each request the runner prints the request, the response with JSON keys sorted, and the service calls your handler made.
hints: For each handler, split the work into three questions: what exactly does the service need from this request, what can the request say that the service must never see, and what exactly may the client see from the service's result?

Look at req.query values: they are always strings, so a page has to pass a digits-only check before you turn it into a number (parseInt accepts "2.5" and "2abc"). Look at where the learner's id can come from (req.user and req.body) and pick the one the client cannot choose. For the response, build a new object field by field instead of starting from the record and removing things.

A similar handler for GET /lessons/:id/comments?offset=&size=: with { offset: "10" } it calls listComments({ lessonId, offset: 10, size: 25 }) using the default size; { size: "300" } becomes size 100 if 100 is the cap; { offset: "-3" } and { size: "2.0" } are 400 with no call; each comment record { id, text, authorId, ipAddress, flagged } becomes { id, text, authorId } in the response.
